cap: A real LAMMPS simulation: 8 caffeine molecules in 3,000 waters. Water is hidden so you can find the caffeines: two fused rings with two C=O groups and three CH3 groups. Grey C, white H, blue N, red O.
Now with all the water. Early in the run the box is about 50 Å wide and the water is loosely packed: about 0.73 g/cm³, well below liquid water (about 1.0).
Pressure and temperature are held constant (NPT), so the box shrank to about 44.5 Å and 1.05 g/cm³, and stays there. Earlier frames are equilibration, normally left out of analysis.
Only waters within 4 Å of a caffeine are shown: roughly the first hydration shell, about 300 of the 3,000. Play and watch waters join and leave.

Cyan dashes: H-bonds (H···acceptor ≤ 2.5 Å, angle ≥ 120°). Caffeine has no O–H or N–H, so it only accepts them. Each C=O oxygen averages about one; N9, the ring N without a CH3, about 0.3. N atoms with a CH3 aren't counted (their lone pairs are shared with the ring).

The same ring carbon in two caffeines: the plot shows their distance (click to jump), the paths their motion. They drift from about 14 to 11 Å apart. Caffeine can stack face to face in water, but no pair does in this short run.
End of the tour. Try other styles, pick atoms to measure, or press Enter VR to walk around the box.
